Submarine production will continue to boost British industry for decades to come backed by the commitments announced in the recent Defence Investment Plan.

Royal Navy First Sea Lord, General Sir Gwyn Jenkins, said:

In an increasingly dangerous world, sea power remains fundamental to keeping our country and people safe. Our submarine fleet is essential to that effort, which is why I am delighted that HMS Agamemnon, the sixth of our Astute-class submarines, has now begun sea trials and will soon arrive at HMNB Clyde to join the fleet. She embodies the best of British engineering and the professionalism of our submariners and will be one of the most advanced submarines ever operated by the Royal Navy. As we continue to strengthen our warfighting readiness, HMS Agamemnon will play a central role in keeping the United Kingdom safe, contributing to NATO’s collective defence and ensuring we are ready to lead, fight and win.

In an increasingly dangerous world, sea power remains fundamental to keeping our country and people safe. Our submarine fleet is essential to that effort, which is why I am delighted that HMS Agamemnon, the sixth of our Astute-class submarines, has now begun sea trials and will soon arrive at HMNB Clyde to join the fleet.

She embodies the best of British engineering and the professionalism of our submariners and will be one of the most advanced submarines ever operated by the Royal Navy.

As we continue to strengthen our warfighting readiness, HMS Agamemnon will play a central role in keeping the United Kingdom safe, contributing to NATO’s collective defence and ensuring we are ready to lead, fight and win.

Building on commitments to continuous submarine production made in the 2025 Strategic Defence Review, and reinforced in the Defence Investment Plan (DIP), the completion of HMS Agamemnon demonstrates the strength and reliability of British industry and its world-leading nuclear technology.

The DIP is backed by £298 billion over the next four years, including £47 billion for investment in our submarine build programmes, which also covers maintenance and infrastructure. Part of that spend will enable the UK to produce a submarine every 18 months in support of the SSN-AUKUS programme.

Recognising Barrow’s role as a strategic national asset, DNE spending is fuelling substantial growth and expansion in the town. The economic certainty from the government’s commitment to the submarine building programme underpins the 10-year Plan for Barrow, backed by the £200 million Barrow Transformation Fund. More than 14,000 roles in Barrow-in-Furness are supported by defence nuclear work, with 1,800 additional roles created in Barrow under this government.

HMS Agamemnon has been delivered as part of a national endeavour by the MOD’s DNE, the partnership organisations that operate, maintain, renew and sustain the UK’s nuclear deterrent. The DNE supports over 47,000 jobs across the UK, including thousands of highly-skilled roles involved in submarine production.

Marking entry into the Royal Navy, HMS Agamemnon was formally commissioned by His Majesty the King in a ceremony on 22 September 2025. She is the sixth Navy vessel to bear the name.

The seventh and final submarine in the class, Achilles, is at an advanced stage of construction in Barrow. The Astute Class will be succeeded by up to 12 new SSN-AUKUS nuclear-powered attack submarines from the late 2030s, with steel due to be cut for the first-in-class in Barrow next year, continuing the town’s role at the heart of AUKUS delivery.
items.titleZh: 第六艘强大的攻击型潜艇离开巴罗因弗内斯进行海试
items.summaryZh: 随着皇家海军第六艘强大的攻击型潜艇从巴罗因弗内斯出发，英国及欧洲-大西洋安全将很快得到加强。
items.zhFull:
最新一艘机敏级潜艇 HMS Agamemnon 已从位于巴罗因弗内斯的 BAE Systems 造船厂驶出。

她现将接受海试——这是向交付这艘能力强大的攻击潜艇、以加强英国和欧洲-大西洋地区安全迈出的重要一步。

在支出审查期间，英国潜艇工业基础正受益于政府 £6 billion 投资，并维持数千个就业岗位。

英国皇家海军最新一艘常规武器核动力潜艇 HMS Agamemnon，绰号“Awesome Aggie”，现将开始海试——这是加入皇家海军现役前的一段测试期。

机敏级是英国皇家海军有史以来操作过的最大、最先进和最强力的攻击潜艇。它们重达 7,400 tonnes，长 97 metres，仅比两个奥林匹克游泳池的长度短一点。该潜艇由在英格兰中部德比生产的罗尔斯·罗伊斯潜艇核反应堆提供动力，在服役期内将无需更换核燃料。

该潜艇的高科技能力包括隐蔽精确打击、反潜战和情报收集。HMS Agamemnon 将配备重型 Spearfish 鱼雷和 Tomahawk IV 对陆攻击导弹，能够打击超过 1,000 miles 范围内的目标。

除了支持持续海上威慑任务外，机敏级潜艇还参与保护海上任务群，并为英国、北约和联军行动提供支持。

首相安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）表示：

亲眼目睹巴罗（Barrow）员工以及英国潜艇供应链数千名员工的奉献与自豪，我深知这一里程碑对他们每一个人将有多么重要。作为有史以来建造的最先进潜艇之一，HMS Agamemnon将在进一步加强我们本土及整个北约的安全方面发挥重要作用。

作为有史以来建造的最先进潜艇之一，HMS Agamemnon将在进一步加强我们本土及整个北约的安全方面发挥重要作用。

国防大臣、议员韦斯·斯特里廷（Wes Streeting）表示：

威慑是我们国家安全的基石。又一艘强大的攻击型潜艇出海，增强了这一威慑，并表明我们正在加大力度应对一个更加危险的世界所带来的威胁。我曾登上HMS Agamemnon，会见了该艇潜艇兵以及完成这一惊人工程壮举的技术工人。这有力提醒我们，加强国防如何创造优质就业、开拓机遇，并推动我国再工业化。

威慑是我们国家安全的基石。又一艘强大的攻击型潜艇出海，增强了这一威慑，并表明我们正在加大力度应对一个更加危险的世界所带来的威胁。

我曾登上HMS Agamemnon，会见了该艇潜艇兵以及完成这一惊人工程壮举的技术工人。这有力提醒我们，加强国防如何创造优质就业、开拓机遇，并推动我国再工业化。

HMS Agamemnon驶离巴罗因弗内斯（Barrow-in-Furness），是一支技能高超的员工队伍多年努力的成果。这包括BAE Systems和国防核企业（Defence Nuclear Enterprise，DNE）的工程师、技术人员和专家，以及将接舰服役的全舰官兵。他们的综合专长反映了巴罗及英国潜艇产业所保持的技能深度。

国防核事务主管玛迪·麦克特南（Maddy McTernan）表示：

HMS Agamemnon的离港对英国国防核事业而言是一个重要时刻，也明确展示了巴罗员工队伍以及更广泛英国供应链的工程与工业卓越实力。在近期《国防投资计划》所宣布承诺的支持下，潜艇生产将在未来数十年继续提振英国工业。

她现将接受海试——这是向交付这艘能力强大的攻击潜艇、以加强英国和欧洲-大西洋地区安全迈出的重要一步。

机敏级是英国皇家海军有史以来操作过的最大、最先进和最强力的攻击潜艇。它们重达 7,400 tonnes，长 97 metres，仅比两个奥林匹克游泳池的长度短一点。该潜艇由在英格兰中部德比生产的罗尔斯·罗伊斯潜艇核反应堆提供动力，在服役期内将无需更换核燃料。

items.title: British companies to access prized Ukraine data to develop AI drone swarms
items.summary: British companies will gain access to extensive battlefield data from Ukraine for the first time to develop new AI models for advanced drone swarms.
items.body:
New AI-enabled drone swarms will be made in Britain, using battlefield data from Ukraine.

Coveted database available to up to 12 UK companies under inaugural competition which will move to testing at pace.

This advanced technology could boost the UK’s ability to deliver supplies and target enemy capabilities, as the Prime Minister’s AI Taskforce puts AI to work to strengthen national security and reindustrialise Britain.

The UK is the first international partner to access Ukraine’s coveted Avengers AI Labs, following a landmark deal struck by Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Zelenskyy in Kyiv. The database holds imagery and video gathered by uncrewed aerial systems in Ukraine, using daylight and thermal sensors, and is used to develop, train and evaluate AI models.

The Ministry of Defence (MOD) is now inviting UK companies to submit proposals for how they would use the data to create AI models for the next generation of battlefield drones. This is the first competition under the UK-Ukraine AI Partnership and could see the creation of models that let drone swarms keep working when communications are degraded or satellite navigation is unavailable.

Drone swarms can fly, swim or drive autonomously, using AI to work together, identify threats and targets and reach decisions, always with appropriate human involvement. For UK forces, that means a small number of sailors, soldiers and aircrew could direct large numbers of drones at once, on tasks from logistics resupply to precise targeting of enemy capabilities and hunting submarines in the North Atlantic.

This comes as the Prime Minister drove forward global work on AI at the UN General Assembly in New York, both to ensure it is being used as a force for good and to maximise opportunities to use the technology to deliver safety and security for people at home. The Prime Minister announced the launch of work between the UK and US on a new AI and Autonomy partnership. This collaboration will help the UK protect critical national infrastructure, from sea lanes to air space – enabling us to detect threats and deter our adversaries using the latest AI technology developed on both sides of the Atlantic.

Defence Secretary, Wes Streeting MP said:

Ukraine is the frontline of freedom for us all. On my recent visit to Kyiv, I saw first-hand the courage and resilience of the Ukrainian people. I also saw the extraordinary innovation which is allowing them to repel Putin’s illegal and unprovoked invasion. This world-first access to real battlefield data will allow British companies to continue pushing the frontier of defence innovation, deterring our enemies and making us safer at home as well as further strengthening Ukraine.

Ukraine is the frontline of freedom for us all. On my recent visit to Kyiv, I saw first-hand the courage and resilience of the Ukrainian people. I also saw the extraordinary innovation which is allowing them to repel Putin’s illegal and unprovoked invasion.

This world-first access to real battlefield data will allow British companies to continue pushing the frontier of defence innovation, deterring our enemies and making us safer at home as well as further strengthening Ukraine.

AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said:

This is the Prime Minister’s AI Taskforce delivering: bringing together Ukraine’s hard-won battlefield experience with Britain’s best AI companies to develop and deploy capabilities faster. It is exactly the kind of practical partnership the Taskforce was set up to drive, supporting our ally Ukraine while strengthening sovereign capability here in Britain.

This is the Prime Minister’s AI Taskforce delivering: bringing together Ukraine’s hard-won battlefield experience with Britain’s best AI companies to develop and deploy capabilities faster.

It is exactly the kind of practical partnership the Taskforce was set up to drive, supporting our ally Ukraine while strengthening sovereign capability here in Britain.

The database includes sensor information from over 6 million detections of objects, such as tanks, artillery, air defence systems, infantry, and aerial targets, including Shahed drones and reconnaissance Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles.

Access to the extensive database will be initially available for up to 12 UK companies and their proposals must be applicable to both Ukrainian and British defence requirements. To advance this work at pace, those companies will be selected in just a matter of weeks and their exploitation of the data is expected to begin soon after.

The work is being led by the MOD’s Taskforce RAID (Rapid AI Delivery) – a team dedicated to ensuring soldiers, sailors and aircrew have access to smarter technology that helps them make better decisions, take on dangerous tasks with less risk, and outpace adversaries who are rapidly developing their own AI capabilities.

The activity demonstrates the Prime Minister’s AI Taskforce turning the Government’s ambitions for AI into real-world capability. Working jointly with the MOD’s Taskforce RAID they are harnessing British expertise to strengthen national security, support our allies and reindustrialise Britain by building the industries of the future here in the UK.

The recent agreement, which forms a key part of the UK and Ukraine’s 100 Year Partnership, underlines the close relationship between both countries to drive global security and stability and ensure Ukraine has the capability and means to defend itself from Russia’s barbaric invasion.

The MOD is seeking innovative proposals covering one or more of the following areas within drone operations:

Autonomous Target Recognition: AI-enabled detection, classification, prioritisation and tracking of operationally relevant objects across complex and contested environments.

Distributed Decision-Making: Enabling multiple autonomous systems to dynamically adapt routes, priorities and behaviours in response to changing battlefield conditions, without relying on a single point of control.

Adaptive Mission Execution: AI approaches enabling multiple autonomous systems to coordinate actions under constrained communications and decentralised control.

Collaborative Sensing and Information Fusion: Methods for sharing, fusing and exploiting information across multiple platforms and sensors to improve situational awareness and mission effectiveness.

For further details about the competition, and to apply, please go to the following: Submission Portal
items.titleZh: 英国企业将获准使用乌克兰珍贵数据开发AI无人机蜂群
items.summaryZh: 英国企业将首次获准使用乌克兰的大量战场数据，用于开发面向先进无人机蜂群的新型AI模型。
items.zhFull:
新型AI赋能的无人机蜂群将在英国制造，使用来自乌克兰的战场数据。

在首次竞赛中，这一令人垂涎的数据库将向最多12家英国公司开放，相关进程将快速转入测试阶段。

这项先进技术可能提升英国投送补给和打击敌方能力的能力，因为首相的AI特别工作组正让AI发挥作用，以加强国家安全并推动英国再工业化。

英国成为首个获准使用乌克兰令人垂涎的Avengers AI Labs的国际伙伴，此前英国首相安迪·伯纳姆 (Andy Burnham) 与总统泽连斯基 (Zelenskyy) 在基辅达成了一项具有里程碑意义的协议。该数据库存有乌克兰无人机系统使用日光和热成像传感器采集的图像和视频，用于开发、训练和评估AI模型。

英国国防部 (MOD) 现在邀请英国公司提交方案，说明它们将如何利用这些数据为下一代战场无人机制作AI模型。这是英乌AI伙伴关系下的首项竞赛，可能催生出这样的模型：在通信降级或卫星导航不可用时，让无人机蜂群仍能继续运作。

无人机蜂群能够自主飞行、游泳或行驶，利用AI协同行动、识别威胁与目标并作出决策，且始终有适当的人工参与。对英国部队而言，这意味着少数水兵、士兵和空勤人员就能同时指挥大量无人机，执行从后勤补给到精确打击敌方能力，再到在北大西洋猎潜等任务。

此时，首相正在纽约联合国大会上推动AI领域的全球工作，既确保AI被用于善途，也最大限度利用该技术为本国民众提供安全保障。首相宣布英国与美国启动一项新的AI与自主性伙伴关系工作。这一合作将帮助英国保护关键国家基础设施，从海上航道到空域，使我们能够利用大西洋两岸开发的最新AI技术探测威胁、威慑对手。

国防大臣韦斯·斯特里廷 (Wes Streeting) 议员表示：

乌克兰是我们所有人自由的前线。在我最近访问基辅期间，我亲眼目睹了乌克兰人民的勇气与韧性。我也看到了非凡的创新，这正使他们能够击退普京非法且无端的入侵。这种全球首次获取真实战场数据的机会，将使英国公司能够继续推进国防创新的前沿，威慑我们的敌人，让我们在国内更安全，并进一步加强乌克兰。

乌克兰是我们所有人自由的前线。在我最近访问基辅期间，我亲眼目睹了乌克兰人民的勇气与韧性。我也看到了非凡的创新，这正使他们能够击退普京非法且无端的入侵。

这种全球首次获取真实战场数据的机会，将使英国公司能够继续推进国防创新的前沿，威慑我们的敌人，让我们在国内更安全，并进一步加强乌克兰。

人工智能大臣卡尼什卡·纳拉扬（Kanishka Narayan）表示：

这正是首相人工智能工作组交出的成果：将乌克兰来之不易的战场经验与英国最优秀的人工智能公司结合起来，以更快地开发和部署能力。这正是该工作组成立之初所要推动的那类务实伙伴关系，既支持我们的盟友乌克兰，又增强英国本土的主权能力。

这正是首相人工智能工作组交出的成果：将乌克兰来之不易的战场经验与英国最优秀的人工智能公司结合起来，以更快地开发和部署能力。

这正是该工作组成立之初所要推动的那类务实伙伴关系，既支持我们的盟友乌克兰，又增强英国本土的主权能力。

该数据库包含来自超过 600 万次目标探测的传感器信息，探测对象包括坦克、火炮、防空系统、步兵和空中目标，其中包括 Shahed 无人机和侦察无人航空器。

该庞大数据库的访问权限最初将向最多12家英国公司开放，其提案必须同时适用于乌克兰和英国的防务需求。为加快这项工作，这些公司将在短短数周内选定，预计其对该数据的利用不久后便会开始。

这项工作由英国国防部的“快速人工智能交付”特别工作组（Taskforce RAID）牵头——该团队致力于确保士兵、水兵和空勤人员能够使用更智能的技术，从而帮助他们做出更好的决策、以更低风险执行危险任务，并领先于正在快速研发自身人工智能能力的对手。

这项活动表明，首相的人工智能特别工作组正将政府对人工智能的雄心转化为现实能力。该工作组与英国国防部的 Taskforce RAID 协同工作，利用英国的专业能力来加强国家安全、支持我们的盟友，并通过在英国本土建设未来产业来实现英国的再工业化。

近期达成的这项协议是英国与乌克兰“百年伙伴关系”的关键组成部分，凸显了两国之间的紧密关系，旨在推动全球安全与稳定，并确保乌克兰拥有抵御俄罗斯野蛮入侵的能力和手段。

英国国防部正在寻求创新提案，涵盖无人机作战中的以下一个或多个领域：

自主目标识别：在复杂且充满对抗的环境中，利用人工智能对与作战相关的目标进行探测、分类、优先级排序和跟踪。

分布式决策：使多个自主系统能够根据不断变化的战场条件动态调整路线、优先级和行为，而不依赖单一控制点。

自适应任务执行：人工智能方法使多个自主系统能够在通信受限和去中心化控制下协调行动。

协同感知与信息融合：跨多个平台和传感器共享、融合和利用信息，以提高态势感知和任务效能的方法。

items.title: CEOs from sensitive sectors to receive briefings on Russia threats
items.summary: CEOs from the most sensitive sectors of the economy will receive closed-door briefings on threats posed by Russia
items.body:
Security Minister Dan Jarvis and Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones to chair closed-door threat-briefings on Russia.

Representatives from Defence and Critical National Infrastructure sectors to be invited to Whitehall.

Comes after the Prime Minister used his speech to the UN General Assembly earlier this week to call out Russia for its hybrid attacks and actions in Ukraine

Critical National Infrastructure providers and defence companies are set to be invited for briefings from security and defence ministers on the threat posed by Russia.

Security Minister Dan Jarvis will chair a threat briefing with industry bodies representing CNI providers, while Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones will chair a threat briefing with industry bodies representing defence firms.

Russia poses an enduring and significant threat to the UK and its interests around the world. The state and its proxies knowingly seek to disrupt businesses and organisations that underpin the British way of life or are vital to the defence of Ukraine. They use tactics like cyber attacks, sabotage and disinformation to take organisations offline, disrupt activity, and weaken trust.

The briefings will draw on world class intelligence capabilities and comes after the Prime Minister used his speech to the UN General Assembly earlier this week to call out Russia for its actions in Ukraine, the UK and elsewhere.

Security Minister, Dan Jarvis, said:

Strong defences are built on a clear understanding of the threat. That’s why I’ll be chairing this briefing, to share world-class intelligence with some of the most important organisations in the country, to ensure they understand and are prepared for the threats we face. We’ll be focusing on the actions they can take in partnership with government, to help keep our country safe.

Strong defences are built on a clear understanding of the threat.

That’s why I’ll be chairing this briefing, to share world-class intelligence with some of the most important organisations in the country, to ensure they understand and are prepared for the threats we face.

We’ll be focusing on the actions they can take in partnership with government, to help keep our country safe.

Minister for the Armed Forces, Louise Sandher-Jones, said:

Russia is actively seeking to disrupt the organisations that form the bedrock of our national security. By bringing government and defence industry leaders together, we can deepen our shared understanding of the threat and strengthen our collective resilience. Protecting our defence sector is essential to keeping Britain secure.

Russia is actively seeking to disrupt the organisations that form the bedrock of our national security.

By bringing government and defence industry leaders together, we can deepen our shared understanding of the threat and strengthen our collective resilience.

Protecting our defence sector is essential to keeping Britain secure.

It follows similar briefings held earlier this year to update university leaders and political parties on the threat of foreign interference and the actions they could take to strengthen national security.

The briefings will sit alongside the support the UK Government already provides to help protect defence firms and Critical National Infrastructure providers from threats, including: specialist policing through organisations like the Civil Nuclear Constabulary; world class cyber expertise through the National Cyber Security Centre; and tailored security advice through the National Protective Security Authority.

Just this month, the Crown Prosecution Service charged a British man with offences under the National Security Act, after he allegedly engaged in conduct to prepare an act of sabotage and received instructions from an individual believed to be linked to the GRU Volunteer Corps.
items.titleZh: 敏感行业首席执行官将听取有关俄罗斯威胁的简报
items.summaryZh: 经济中最为敏感行业的首席执行官将就俄罗斯构成的威胁接受闭门简报。
items.zhFull:
安全大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）和武装部队大臣路易丝·桑德-琼斯（Louise Sandher-Jones）将主持关于俄罗斯的闭门威胁简报会。

国防和关键国家基础设施领域的代表将受邀前往白厅。

此前，首相在本周早些时候向联合国大会发表演讲时，点名批评俄罗斯的混合攻击及其在乌克兰的行动。

关键国家基础设施供应商和国防企业将受邀参加安全与国防大臣就俄罗斯所构成威胁举行的简报会。

安全大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）将主持一场与代表关键国家基础设施供应商的行业机构进行的威胁简报会，武装部队大臣路易丝·桑德-琼斯（Louise Sandher-Jones）则将主持一场与代表国防企业的行业机构进行的威胁简报会。

俄罗斯对英国及其在世界各地的利益构成持久而重大的威胁。该国及其代理人蓄意寻求破坏支撑英国生活方式、或对乌克兰防御至关重要的企业和组织。他们使用网络攻击、破坏活动和虚假信息等手法，使相关组织断网下线、扰乱其活动并削弱信任。

这些简报会将依托世界一流的情报能力，此前首相在本周早些时候向联合国大会发表演讲时，点名批评俄罗斯在乌克兰、英国及其他地区的行动。

安全大臣丹·贾维斯（Dan Jarvis）表示：

牢固的防御建立在清楚认识威胁的基础上。正因如此，我将主持这次简报会，与国内一些最重要的机构分享世界级情报，确保他们了解并准备好应对我们所面临的威胁。我们将重点讨论他们可与政府合作采取的行动，以帮助维护国家安全。

牢固的防御建立在清楚认识威胁的基础上。

正因如此，我将主持这次简报会，与国内一些最重要的机构分享世界级情报，确保他们了解并准备好应对我们所面临的威胁。

我们将重点讨论他们可与政府合作采取的行动，以帮助维护国家安全。

武装部队国务大臣路易丝·桑德-琼斯（Louise Sandher-Jones）表示：

俄罗斯正积极寻求破坏构成我们国家安全基石的组织。通过将政府和国防工业领导人聚集在一起，我们可以加深对威胁的共同理解，并增强我们的集体韧性。保护我们的国防部门对保障英国安全至关重要。

俄罗斯正积极寻求破坏构成我们国家安全基石的组织。

通过将政府和国防工业领导人聚集在一起，我们可以加深对威胁的共同理解，并增强我们的集体韧性。

保护我们的国防产业对保障英国安全至关重要。

此次通报之前，今年早些时候已举行过类似通报会，向大学领导人和各政党通报外国干涉的威胁以及他们可采取哪些行动来加强国家安全。

这些通报会将与英国政府已提供的支持共同发挥作用，帮助保护国防企业和关键国家基础设施提供商免受威胁，这些支持包括：通过民用核警察局等机构提供的专业警务；通过国家网络安全中心提供的世界一流网络专业知识；以及通过国家保护安全局提供的量身定制安全建议。

就在本月，英国皇家检察署依据《国家安全法》指控一名英国男子犯有相关罪行，此前他涉嫌从事准备实施破坏行动的行为，并接受了一名据信与GRU志愿军团有关联的人员的指示。

items.title: Guidance: TF RAID Avengers: AI swarming competition
items.summary: The Rapid AI Delivery Taskforce (TF RAID) is running a competition to access Ukraine’s Avengers Labs platform to enhance autonomous drone swarming and collaborative drone operations.
items.body:
TF RAID Avengers: AI swarming competition

The Rapid AI Delivery Taskforce (TF RAID) is running a competition to access Ukraine’s Avengers Labs platform to enhance autonomous drone swarming and collaborative drone operations.

Ministry of Defence

25 September 2026

TF RAID Avengers: AI swarming competition overview

PDF , 1.84 MB , 7 pages

MS Word Document , 5.88 MB

This file is in an OpenDocument format

The Rapid AI Delivery Taskforce (TF RAID) is running an open competition inviting proposals from UK industry on how to use new access to Avengers Labs datasets to enhance autonomous drone swarming and collaborative drone operations. Proposals should have the potential to benefit both UK and Ukrainian armed forces.

Avengers Labs is a Ukrainian government platform containing imagery and footage of various ground and aerial targets collected in Ukraine. This is the inaugural competition under the UK-Ukraine AI partnership.

How to apply

Read the competition overview document to understand the challenge requirements.

Answer all of the questions outlined in the submission template.

Submit your PDF proposal addressing the challenge requirements through the submission portal.

competition launch date: 25 September 2026

briefing call to UK industry: 7 October 2026

deadline for submissions: 11:59pm BST on 22 October 2026

MOD review of submissions and companies: 23 to 30 October 2026

selected companies for Phase 1 access to Avengers Labs notified: by 6 November 2026

items.title: Long-Term Growth in Child Mental Health Expenditures, 2004-2023
items.author: Hao Yu
items.summary: This paper estimates trends in mental health expenditures, probability of use and expenditures per user for US children aged 2-17 from 2004 to 2023.
items.body:
ResearchPosted on rand.org Sep 25, 2026Published in: Health Affairs Scholar, qxag250 (2026). DOI: 10.1093/haschl/qxag250

Investment in mental health treatment for children has grown substantially, but whether this reflects more treatment recipients, higher spending per user, or both has not been examined.

To estimate trends in mental health expenditures, probability of use and expenditures per user for US children aged 2–17 from 2004 to 2023.

Two-part models were estimated to predict inflation adjusted health expenditure data from the 2004-2023 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (unweighted N=153,622) to assess overall trends and variation by age-group and insurance coverage.

Total annual mental health expenditures increased from $10.9B to $37.9B, rising from 4.4% to 8.1% of total health expenditure per child (mean individual-level ratio among children with any health care expenditure). The probability of mental health service use more than doubled (6.3% to 13.0%, +0.35 percentage points/year), while expenditure per user grew from $2,816 to $5,178 (+3.3%/year). Relative to the 2004 baseline those age 2-5 had the greatest growth in both service use and expenditure per user. Expenditure per user grew substantially faster for privately-insured than for Medicaid-covered children.

Child mental health treatment expenditures have grown dramatically over the past two decades, with particularly large increases for those ages two to five.

items.titleZh: 2004至2023年儿童心理健康支出的长期增长
items.summaryZh: 本文估算了2004年至2023年美国2至17岁儿童心理健康支出的趋势、使用概率以及每名使用者的支出。
items.zhFull:
研究发布于 rand.org，2026年9月25日；发表于：Health Affairs Scholar, qxag250 (2026)。DOI: 10.1093/haschl/qxag250

儿童心理健康治疗投资大幅增长，但这反映的是治疗接受者更多、每名使用者支出更高，还是两者兼有，尚未得到考察。

旨在估计2004年至2023年美国2—17岁儿童在心理健康支出、使用概率和每名使用者支出方面的趋势。

拟合两部分模型，以预测2004—2023年 Medical Expenditure Panel Survey（未加权 N=153,622）中经通胀调整的卫生支出数据，并评估总体趋势以及按年龄组和保险覆盖情况划分的差异。

年度心理健康总支出从 $10.9B 增至 $37.9B，占每名儿童总卫生支出的比例从 4.4% 升至 8.1%（在任何卫生保健支出的儿童中，个体层面比例的平均值）。心理健康服务使用概率增加了一倍以上（从 6.3% 升至 13.0%，每年增加 0.35 个百分点），而每名使用者的支出从 $2,816 增至 $5,178（每年增长 3.3%）。相对于2004年基线，2—5岁儿童在服务使用和每名使用者支出两方面的增幅均最大。私人保险儿童每名使用者的支出增长显著快于 Medicaid 覆盖儿童。

过去二十年，儿童心理健康治疗支出急剧增长，其中2至5岁儿童的增幅尤其大。

items.title: McChord Encourages Rider Mentorship Through Motorcycle Safety Program
items.author: SrA Benjamin Riddle
items.summary: The 62d Airlift Wing hosted a Department of the Air Force Rider Mentor Program trainer course at Heritage Hill on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Sept. 8-9, 2026. The program supports the mandatory motorcycle training requirements of Level II training within one year of earning a Level I initial license and Level III refresher training every five years after. The program takes care to emphasize the decisions that affect rider safety the most.
items.body: The 62d Airlift Wing hosted a Department of the Air Force Rider Mentor Program trainer course at Heritage Hill on Joint Base Lewis-McChord, Washington, Sept. 8-9, 2026. Seven riders from multiple squadrons completed the course, including two members of the 142nd Wing, Oregon Air National Guard. The newly trained mentors will help expand local access to motorcycle safety training and assist experienced riders with mentoring others in their units. The program supports the mandatory motorcycle training requirements of Level II training within one year of earning a Level I initial license and Level III refresher training every five years after. The program takes care to emphasize the decisions that affect rider safety the most. “It comes down to what gets our guardians and our airmen injured, hurt, or killed,” said John McLaughlin, Air Force Safety Center deputy chief of traffic safety and outreach. “It’s the decision making, the behaviors that they’re using while they’re out on motorcycles.” McLaughlin highlighted how the program will be able to give units a more direct path to required training. “This training is a supplement to the current training and an alternative way of acquiring those skills across the DAF,” said McLaughlin. “This program will make it so here at JBLM, training can be done at the squadron level, and you don’t have to go all the way to the installation level to get training.” Before this new program, Air Force riders at JBLM would often need to coordinate through their motorcycle safety representatives, who would coordinate through wing safety who would then schedule training with the Army. The new mentor network will allow MSRs to provide instruction directly to the riders who need it. The course critically prepares mentors to lead discussions and practical exercises that reinforce riding fundamentals, sound judgment and risk management. The program also creates opportunities for riders to learn from one another’s experiences, said McLaughlin. “I can share stories to help others learn so they don’t have to go through some of the experiences I went through,” said McLaughlin. “That’s the main point of the program, current riders mentoring newer and older riders alike to all learn together.” Tech. Sgt. Corey Walrath, 62d Aircraft Maintenance Squadron squadron program manager, who helped bring McLaughlin to JBLM, said the local program gives the wing flexibility to meet increased demands for training. “With the rider mentor program, now Airmen can come to their MSRs or me for the 62d AMXS, and we can come up with a schedule that works for them right then and there,” said Walrath. “This will be able to quickly get them the training they need to stay safe on the roads.” Staff Sgt. Garrett Cofield, 62d Aerial Port Squadron passenger service supervisor, gave his thoughts on how the course reinforced the value of continuing to learn, regardless of experience level. “When I was doing the Level II, I thought I was a really good rider, I was a lot younger and I had a much bigger ego,” said Cofield. “I think coming to these trainings and learning the fundamentals and setting your ego aside is super important.” Ryan Meeks, 62d Airlift Wing occupational safety technician, took time to further highlight the critical nature of the program throughout the DAF. “Inexperienced riders are our primary concern as they account for 90% of the fatalities that the Airforce experiences,” said Meeks “Experienced riders can teach advanced riding techniques, but they also teach awareness, safety, temperament, and maturity factors. Having a trained and experienced rider mentor that you personally know or work with creates an environment of trust and familiarity that cannot be gained in a short class.” The continued growth of the program currently depends on experienced riders stepping forward to mentoring others and leading their unit is fundamental safety, said McLaughlin. If you are interested in becoming an MSR, rider mentor, or rider mentor instructor please contact the wing safety office today at 253-982-9999.
items.titleZh: 麦科德基地通过摩托车安全项目鼓励骑手导师带教
items.summaryZh: 2026年9月8日至9日，第62空运联队在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地的Heritage Hill举办了空军部骑手导师项目教官课程。该项目支持强制性摩托车培训要求，即在取得一级初始驾照后一年内完成二级培训，此后每五年完成三级复训。该项目着重强调对骑手安全影响最大的各项决定。
items.zhFull: 第62空运联队于2026年9月8日至9日在华盛顿州刘易斯-麦科德联合基地（JBLM）的Heritage Hill主办了空军部骑手导师计划教官培训课程。来自多个中队的7名骑手完成了课程，其中包括俄勒冈州空军国民警卫队第142联队的2名成员。新受训的导师将帮助扩大当地获得摩托车安全培训的渠道，并协助经验丰富的骑手指导其所在单位的其他人。该计划支持强制性摩托车培训要求，即在获得I级初始驾照后一年内完成II级培训，此后每五年进行一次III级复训。该计划注重强调对骑手安全影响最大的决策。“归根结底，问题在于是什么导致我们的守护者和空军人员受伤、受到伤害或丧生，”空军安全中心交通安全与外联副主任约翰·麦克劳克林（John McLaughlin）说。“是决策，是他们在骑摩托车时所采取的行为。”麦克劳克林强调，该计划将能够为单位提供更直接的所需培训途径。“这项培训是对现有培训的补充，也是在整个空军部获得这些技能的另一种途径，”麦克劳克林说。“该计划将使得在JBLM这里，培训可以在中队一级完成，你不必一路到基地层级去接受培训。”在这项新计划之前，JBLM的空军骑手通常需要通过他们的摩托车安全代表进行协调，而摩托车安全代表则要通过联队安全部门协调，后者再与陆军安排培训。新的导师网络将使MSR能够直接向需要培训的骑手提供指导。该课程至关重要地培养导师引导讨论和实操练习的能力，以强化骑行基本功、正确判断和风险管理。麦克劳克林说，该计划还为骑手创造了从彼此经验中学习的机会。“我可以分享故事来帮助他人学习，这样他们就不必经历我经历过的一些事情，”麦克劳克林说。“这就是该计划的主旨：现有骑手指导新老骑手，让大家共同学习。”Tech. Sgt. 科里·沃尔拉斯（Corey Walrath），第62飞机维修中队项目主管，曾帮助将麦克劳克林请到JBLM，他说，当地计划使该联队能够灵活满足日益增长的培训需求。“有了骑手导师计划，现在空军人员可以来找他们的MSR，或者来找我（第62飞机维修中队），我们可以当场制定适合他们的安排，”沃尔拉斯说。“这样就能迅速让他们获得在道路上保持安全所需的培训。”Staff Sgt. 加勒特·科菲尔德（Garrett Cofield），第62空中港口中队旅客服务主管，谈到了该课程如何强化了无论经验水平如何都应继续学习的价值。“我参加II级培训时，以为自己是一名非常优秀的骑手，那时我年轻得多，也自负得多，”科菲尔德说。“我认为参加这些培训、学习基本功并放下自负非常重要。”瑞安·米克斯（Ryan Meeks），第62空运联队职业安全技术员，特意进一步强调该计划在整个空军部的关键性质。“经验不足的骑手是我们的首要关切，因为他们占空军所经历死亡事故的90%，”米克斯说。“经验丰富的骑手可以教授高级骑行技术，但他们也传授意识、安全、性情和成熟度等方面的因素。拥有一名你个人认识或共事过的、训练有素且经验丰富的骑手导师，会营造出一种信任和熟悉的氛围，这是短期课程无法获得的。”麦克劳克林说，该计划的持续发展目前取决于经验丰富的骑手挺身而出去指导他人，并带领其单位做好基本安全。如果你有兴趣成为MSR、骑手导师或骑手导师教官，请立即致电253-982-9999联系联队安全办公室。

items.title: Collaborative Combat Aircraft arrive at Creech AFB, advancing operational integration
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: The aircraft will undergo Air Combat Command-led operational experimentation to evaluate uncrewed systems and refine operational employment alongside crewed combat aircraft.
items.body:
Published Sept. 24, 2026

Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs

The Air Force received its first two Collaborative Combat Aircraft at Creech Air Force Base , Nevada, marking a significant step toward integrating uncrewed, semi-autonomous aircraft into future combat operations. Anduril delivered the first CCA, the YFQ-44A, to the Experimental Operations Unit last month, and General Atomics delivered the YFQ-42A last week. The aircraft will support Air Combat Command -led operational experimentation to refine how CCA will be employed alongside crewed aircraft in contested environments.

items.title: Department of the Air Force pilot program expands to help more military spouses
items.author: Jennifer Gonzalez
items.summary: Administered by the AFPC and AFCS, the initiative connects active-duty spouses undergoing a permanent change of station with direct hiring opportunities.
items.body:
Published Sept. 23, 2026

By Jennifer Gonzalez

Air Force Personnel Center

A professional in her own right, Kayla Amie holds a master’s degree in organizational leadership and a Bachelor of Science in education, and has worked steadily since she was legally old enough to hold a job. But when she married a U.S. Air Force Airman, that professional background no longer guaranteed a career and steady income. “Every four years you are starting from scratch. I am ok with pivoting but it’s going from the fact that you worked so hard—being a professional—and having it taken away with each move and it not being your choice,” said Amie.

Luke AFB, Arizona

Goodfellow AFB, Texas

Laughlin AFB, Texas

Mountain Home AFB, Idaho

Travis AFB, California

Patrick SFB, Florida

Ramstein AB, Ramstein-Miesenbach

RAF Croughton, Northamptonshire

RAF Mildenhall, Suffolk

RAF Lakenheath, Suffolk

RAF Feltwell, Norfolk

Kadena AB, Okinawa

Only active-duty military spouses PCSing to the listed bases currently qualify to use the pilot program. Qualified spouses can enroll at any time into the GMSC Program using the Air Force Civilian Service website here .

items.title: DM Airmen participate in Coyote Storm 26.2 to reinforce AEW 2.0 concepts
items.author: Capt. M. Anna Turpin
items.summary: The multi-day training event operationalized Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concepts across cross-functional disciplines, including field medicine, combat search and rescue, and command and control.
items.body:
Published Sept. 22, 2026

By Capt. M. Anna Turpin

355th Wing Public Affairs

Airmen from the 355th Wing strengthened their ability to operate in contested environments during Coyote Storm 26.2 at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base , Sept. 14-17. Coyote Storm 26.2 was a training exercise focused on improving flexibility and readiness through the Air Expeditionary Wing 2.0 concept. AEW 2.0 training requires that preparation for deployments happens long before members go into theater and ensures that they have the time to train together across disciplines.

items.body:
DAYTON, Ohio (AFLCMC) -- “You are part of the fight,” Lt. Gen. Jason Voorheis, commander of the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) told attendees at the Ohio Defense and Aerospace Forum earlier this week. “ General Dale White [Director, Critical Major Weapon Systems at the Pentagon] is fond of saying that militaries don't go to war - nations go to war. You all are part of what our nation brings to the fight in terms of developing fielding and getting capability into the hands of our warfighters.”

Voorheis spoke as part of a panel titled “Power Projection from the Heartland.” He was joined on stage by Brig. Gen. Timothy Helfrich, AFLCMC Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for Fighters and Advanced Aircraft, alongside defense industry professionals TK Kubit and Anthony Cain. JP Nauseef of JobsOhio moderated the discussion. The forum was hosted by the Dayton Development Coalition.

Held at Wright State University on September 21, 2026, the forum highlighted the strategic alignment between Air Force modernization priorities and the Ohio defense ecosystem.

Acquisition Speed and Agility

The Ohio Defense Ecosystem

Workforce and Talent Development

In his opening remarks, Voorheis explained the Air Force acquisition workforce's shift to accept risk earlier, lean into commercial technology and open mission systems, and empower program teams to make decisions that drive projects forward.

Both Voorheis and Helfrich noted that acquisition teams at Wright-Patt and across the Center are transitioning away from platform-specific "stovepipes" to focus on broader, integrated capabilities across advanced aircraft. These teams are also balancing intensive current fleet modernization with future systems development by shifting from individual platform upgrades to an integrated, "system of systems" approach.

“I think one of the really important parts about the acquisition transformation is the change in philosophy and focus on delivering fielded capability as kind of the preeminent prioritized pacing thing that we do, and everything else is about how we achieve that to include the authorities we're giving PAEs,” noted Voorheis.

Helfrich’s Fighters and Advanced Aircraft portfolio includes the A-10, F-15, F-16, F-22, plus the FQ-42, FQ-44, other collaborative combat aircraft.

The Air Force Research Lab (AFRL) is also headquartered at Wright-Patt. Helfrich touted how AFRL led key advances in open architecture and credits AFRL with developing the Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) program.

“There would be no CCA without the Air Force Research Laboratory,” explained Helfrich. “Both the FQ-42 Vengeance [and] the FQ-44 Fury were heavily invested in by AFRL. Because software is sold separately with CCA, the mission autonomy work started at AFRL. They were really the ones who put together the first consortium to build Autonomous Government Reference Architecture (A-GRA). This has become a huge program, all made possible because of the investments by AFRL.”

For both Voorheis and Helfrich, the workforce and supporting infrastructure remain top concerns. Helfrich urged educators in the audience to modernize military engineering and software development classes. Both speakers noted the shortage of physical defense infrastructure in the area around Wright-Patterson, particularly for high-level classified work.

In addition to physical plant limitations, hiring remains a challenge. AFLCMC currently has over 1,700 vacancies , with more than half located at Wright-Patt. Most open positions are in technical fields like engineering and logistics. Business areas like contracting and program management also have many openings.

“We need help recruiting from the universities and from industry as well, both defense industry and non-defense industry,” explained Voorheis. “You don't have to come in with a lot of aerospace experience. What we really need is highly talented, motivated, critical thinkers.”

The panel marked the first time Lt. Gen. Voorheis has publicly spoken about his role leading AFLCMC since assuming command late last month .
items.titleZh: AFLCMC司令在俄亥俄州国防与航空航天论坛上阐述采办优先事项
items.summaryZh: 俄亥俄州代顿（AFLCMC）——“你们也是这场战斗的一部分，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）司令Lt. Gen.贾森·沃希斯（Jason Voorheis）本周早些时候在俄亥俄州国防与航空航天论坛上对与会者表示。“Gen.戴尔·怀特（五角大楼关键重大武器系统主管）喜欢说，参战的不是军队——而是国家。你们所有人都是我们国家投入这场战斗的一部分，体现在研发、列装并把能力交到我们的……手中。”
items.zhFull:
代顿，俄亥俄州（AFLCMC）——“你们是战斗的一部分，”美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）司令 Lt. Gen. 贾森·沃里斯（Jason Voorheis）本周早些时候在俄亥俄国防与航空航天论坛上对与会者说。“戴尔·怀特将军（Dale White）[五角大楼关键重大武器系统主管]喜欢说，军队不会开战——国家才会开战。你们所有人都是我国为这场战斗所贡献力量的一部分，无论是开发、列装，还是把能力交到我们的作战人员手中。”

沃里斯作为题为“来自腹地的力量投射”的专题讨论小组成员发言。与他同台的有 Brig. Gen. 蒂莫西·赫尔弗里希（Timothy Helfrich），AFLCMC 战斗机与先进飞机组合采办执行官（PAE），以及国防工业专业人士 TK·库比特（TK Kubit）和安东尼·凯恩（Anthony Cain）。JobsOhio 的 JP·诺西夫（JP Nauseef）主持了讨论。该论坛由代顿发展联盟主办。

论坛于2026年9月21日在莱特州立大学举行，凸显了空军现代化优先事项与俄亥俄国防生态系统之间的战略协同。

采办速度与敏捷性

俄亥俄国防生态系统

劳动力与人才发展

沃里斯在开场致辞中解释说，空军采办队伍正在转变，更早接受风险，积极采用商业技术和开放任务系统，并赋予项目团队作出推动项目前进的决策的权力。

沃里斯和赫尔弗里希都指出，Wright-Patt 以及整个中心的采办团队正从针对特定平台的“烟囱式”模式转向，专注于先进飞机更广泛的一体化能力。这些团队还在平衡当前密集的机队现代化与未来系统开发，从单个平台升级转向一体化的“系统之系统”方法。

“我认为采办转型真正重要的部分之一，是理念的转变，以及把交付已列装能力作为我们最重要的优先事项和节奏牵引，而其他一切——包括我们赋予PAE的权限——都是为了实现这一目标，”沃海斯（Voorheis）指出。

赫尔弗里希（Helfrich）的“战斗机与先进飞机”组合包括A-10、F-15、F-16、F-22，以及FQ-42、FQ-44和其他协同作战飞机。

美国空军研究实验室（AFRL）也总部设在赖特-帕特森（Wright-Patt）。赫尔弗里希盛赞AFRL在开放架构方面引领了关键进展，并将协同作战飞机（CCA）项目的发展归功于AFRL。

“没有美国空军研究实验室，就不会有CCA，”赫尔弗里希解释道。“AFRL对FQ-42‘复仇’和FQ-44‘狂怒’都投入了大量资金。由于CCA的软件是单独销售的，任务自主性工作始于AFRL。他们确实是组建首个联盟来构建自主政府参考架构（A-GRA）的一方。这已成为一个庞大的项目，而这一切都得益于AFRL的投资。”

对沃海斯和赫尔弗里希而言，劳动力和配套基础设施仍是首要关切。赫尔弗里希敦促在场教育工作者对军事工程和软件开发课程进行现代化改革。两位发言人都指出，赖特-帕特森周边地区缺乏实体国防基础设施，尤其是用于高级别机密工作的设施。

除实体设施限制外，招聘仍是一项挑战。美国空军生命周期管理中心（AFLCMC）目前有超过1,700个职位空缺，其中一半以上位于赖特-帕特森。大多数空缺职位属于工程和后勤等技术领域。合同签订和项目管理等业务领域也有许多空缺。

“我们需要在从大学以及产业界招聘方面获得帮助，既包括国防产业，也包括非国防产业，”沃海斯解释道。“你不需要带着丰富的航空航天经验入职。我们真正需要的是才华出众、积极进取、善于批判性思考的人。”

此次小组讨论标志着Lt. Gen.沃海斯自上月底就任指挥官以来，首次公开谈及他领导AFLCMC的职责。

items.title: AFSOC proves Havoc Spear precise, effective
items.author: Pentagon News
items.summary: AFSOC announced its small cruise missile, the AGM-190A Havoc Spear, has been evaluated in a test configuration and successfully meets requirements to become an available weapons system for broader real-world use across a variety of special operations and conventional aircraft.
items.body:
Published Sept. 22, 2026

Air Force Special Operations Command Public Affairs

Air Force Special Operations Command announced its small cruise missile, the AGM-190A Havoc Spear, has been evaluated in a test configuration and successfully meets requirements to become an available weapon system for broader real-world use across a variety of special operations and conventional aircraft.

items.titleZh: AFSOC验证Havoc Spear精确且有效
items.summaryZh: 美国空军特种作战司令部（AFSOC）宣布，其小型巡航导弹AGM-190A Havoc Spear已在一种试验构型下完成评估，并成功满足相关要求，可作为一种可用的武器系统，在各类特种作战飞机和常规飞机上更广泛地投入实际使用。

items.title: Netanyahu May Have Ignored a Dire Warning. Israel Ignores the Deeper Threat.
items.summary: Israel's strategy in Gaza is only keeping Hamas in power: deterred, but not replaced, with no real alternative given a chance. A different outcome calls for a different approach.
items.body:
Israelis are still debating whether the recent report is true—whether the United Arab Emirates warned Israel of an imminent Hamas attack roughly 10 days before the Oct. 7 massacre.

But fixating on the few days before Oct. 7 obscures a deeper flaw: The Israeli mindset, the strategic conception, remains largely unchanged. It is conflict management. Israel is using a weakened and deterred Hamas ruling Gaza as an excuse to deepen the divide between Gaza and a Palestinian Authority–run West Bank. By avoiding allowing any alternative to emerge, it is sidelining the Palestinian question altogether.

If the deadliest disaster of Jews since the Holocaust should have changed one thing, it was this. Yet, strip away the rhetoric of “total victory,” and Israel’s Gaza policy today looks quite similar, just with more bloodshed and rubble.

In recent weeks, Israeli leaders have vowed to remain in Gaza for the long term and end Hamas’s rule once and for all. Following a string of successful assassinations of Hamas commanders, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz declared: “Our message is clear: No terrorist is immune, and Hamas will not be in Gaza.”

Israel is using a weakened and deterred Hamas ruling Gaza as an excuse to deepen the divide between Gaza and a Palestinian Authority–run West Bank.

Weakening Hamas is legitimate, and so is Israel’s demand that it relinquish control of Gaza. But Israel’s revealed preference tells a different story.

Even as Israel holds an estimated 60 percent of Gaza, Hamas still controls over 95 percent of the population. Hamas is both a terrorist organization and Gaza’s de facto government; removing the former requires an alternative for the latter. Israel refused to hand that role to the Palestinian Authority but signed on to President Trump’s 20-point plan last year, which offers exactly that: a transition to the technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, eventually leading to a reformed Palestinian Authority.

The Israeli government apparently never intended to let that alternative emerge.

Members of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza remain in Cairo, with no timeline for entering Gaza. Roughly 6,000 vetted police recruits, meant to begin training months ago, have not left Gaza because Israel will not commit to letting them return.

Construction of a base for the International Stabilization Force is stalled by bureaucracy. Reconstruction of the Israeli-held “Green Zone” meant to showcase non-Hamas governance hasn’t advanced. And in the West Bank, Israeli policy is weakening the Palestinian Authority toward collapse and carving the territory into cantons to ensure no Palestinian governance, with or without Gaza, is ever viable.

Hamas has expectedly stalled the plan, too. But in August it accepted the Board of Peace’s roadmap, listing 15 principles for phased disarmament in exchange for Israel Defense Forces withdrawal. Israel has valid concerns, including the roadmap’s timeline, scope of disarmament, and Qatar and Turkey’s role in verifying compliance.

A future Israeli government that wants a different outcome will have to act like it.

But justified skepticism does not excuse refusing to engage. Instead of making Hamas back its words, Israel has effectively handed it veto power over the process, drawing international blame for stalling while Hamas gains recognition as a legitimate partner.

Domestic politics explains much of this. Israel faces a charged election on Oct. 27, and Netanyahu’s coalition cannot show compromise on Gaza. Even pressure from Trump plays in his favor, as he claims to be the only one who can stand up to who he called “the greatest friend that the state of Israel has ever had in the White House.” Netanyahu’s rivals, meantime, are trying to outflank him from the right, vowing to keep fighting rather than engage the U.S.-led plan.

But whoever wins will still have to pick up the Trump framework. The alternatives—renewed full-scale war or a Gaza permanently split between an Israeli-held east and Hamas-run west—serve neither Israel’s security interests nor produce an acceptable status quo.

Rather than campaigning on the same hawkish instinct, prime minister contenders should say that the current approach only keeps Hamas in power: deterred, but not replaced, with no real alternative given a chance.

A future Israeli government that wants a different outcome will have to act like it. This means setting a political horizon instead of managing the conflict incident by incident, taking initiative on the Trump plan and disarmament roadmap instead of being dragged along by Washington, Cairo, or Doha.

It also requires letting the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza function and supporting Palestinian Authority reform rather than treating its flaws as a pretext for exclusion and redirecting Gaza’s financial lifelines to starve Hamas economically rather than merely bombing it.

Such a shift could unlock the funding, troops, and regional cooperation the plan needs, and begin restoring Israel’s ties with Europe and the Arab world.

A new government will find it hard to change course quickly. The only way to make that happen is U.S. leadership from the top, because whoever wins will want Trump on their side.

The ceasefire, the hostages’ return, and the 20-point framework a year ago were a major achievement. The Trump administration can use this anniversary and Israel’s election to press ahead. Otherwise, Israel risks drifting back into an Oct. 6 reality: a contained, managed Hamas quietly rebuilding behind a calm facade, primed to explode again.
items.titleZh: 内塔尼亚胡（Netanyahu）或许忽视了一个严峻警告。以色列则忽视了更深层的威胁。
items.summaryZh: 以色列在加沙的战略只会让哈马斯继续掌权：受到威慑却未被取代，也没有任何真正的替代方案获得机会。要得到不同的结果，就需要不同的做法。
items.zhFull:
以色列人仍在争论，最近的那则报道是否属实——阿拉伯联合酋长国是否在10月7日屠杀发生前约10天，就警告过以色列哈马斯即将发动袭击。

但把目光死盯在10月7日之前的这几天上，会掩盖一个更深层的缺陷：以色列人的思维方式和战略构想基本没有改变，那就是冲突管理。以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。通过不让任何替代方案出现，它把巴勒斯坦问题整个边缘化了。

如果说大屠杀以来犹太人遭遇的最惨重灾难本应改变一件事，那就应该是这一点。然而，剥去“全面胜利”的说辞，以色列今天的加沙政策看上去并无二致，只是流血更多、废墟更多。

近几周，以色列领导人誓言要长期留在加沙，并彻底终结哈马斯的统治。在接连成功暗杀哈马斯指挥官之后，总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）和国防部长伊斯雷尔·卡茨（Israel Katz）宣称：“我们的信息很明确：没有哪个恐怖分子可以豁免，哈马斯不会留在加沙。”

以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。

削弱哈马斯是正当的，以色列要求其放弃对加沙的控制也是正当的。但以色列显露出的实际偏好却讲述了另一个故事。

尽管以色列控制着加沙约60%的地区，哈马斯仍控制着当地95%以上的人口。哈马斯既是恐怖组织，也是加沙事实上的政府；要铲除前者，就必须为后者提供替代方案。以色列拒绝把这一角色交给巴勒斯坦权力机构，但去年却签署了特朗普（Trump）总统的20点计划，而该计划提供的正是这一点：过渡到技术官僚性质的加沙行政管理全国委员会，最终走向改革后的巴勒斯坦权力机构。

以色列政府显然从未打算让这一替代方案出现。

加沙管理国家委员会成员仍留在开罗，没有进入加沙的时间表。大约6000名经过审查的警察新兵本应在数月前开始训练，但因以色列不愿承诺允许他们返回，至今未能离开加沙。

国际稳定部队基地的建设因官僚程序而停滞。以色列控制的“绿区”本意是展示非哈马斯治理，其重建毫无进展。在约旦河西岸，以色列的政策正削弱巴勒斯坦权力机构，使其走向崩溃，并将该地区切割成一块块飞地，以确保无论有无加沙，巴勒斯坦治理都永远无法可行。

哈马斯也不出所料地拖延了这一计划。但8月它接受了和平委员会的路线图，列出15项原则，以分阶段解除武装换取以色列国防军撤离。以色列的担忧不无道理，包括路线图的时间表、解除武装的范围，以及卡塔尔和土耳其在核查遵守情况方面的作用。

未来的以色列政府若想取得不同的结果，就必须以相应的方式行事。

但合理的怀疑并不能成为拒绝接触的借口。以色列没有迫使哈马斯兑现其言辞，反而实际上赋予其对这一进程的否决权，因拖延而招致国际指责，而哈马斯则获得合法伙伴的认可。

国内政治在很大程度上解释了这一切。以色列将于10月27日举行一场激烈的选举，内塔尼亚胡的联盟无法在加沙问题上展现妥协。就连特朗普施压也对他有利，因为他声称只有他才能顶住他所称的“以色列国在白宫有史以来最伟大的朋友”。与此同时，内塔尼亚胡的对手正试图从右翼包抄他，誓言继续战斗，而非参与美国主导的计划。

但无论谁获胜，都仍须接过特朗普的框架。其他选项——重启全面战争，或加沙永久分裂为以色列控制的东部和哈马斯控制的西部——既不符合以色列的安全利益，也无法形成可接受的现状。

总理职位角逐者不应以同样的鹰派本能进行竞选，而应指出：当前做法只会让哈马斯继续掌权——受到威慑，却未被取代，真正的替代方案从未获得机会。

未来一个想要不同结果的以色列政府，就必须以相应的方式行事。这意味着要设定政治前景，而不是逐次事件地管控冲突；要在特朗普计划和解除武装路线图上采取主动，而不是被华盛顿、开罗或多哈牵着走。

这还要求让加沙管理全国委员会能够运作，并支持巴勒斯坦权力机构改革，而不是将其缺陷当作排斥的借口，并将加沙的资金命脉转向在经济上扼杀哈马斯，而不只是对其进行轰炸。

这样的转变可能释放该计划所需的资金、部队和区域合作，并开始恢复以色列与欧洲和阿拉伯世界的关系。

新政府将很难迅速改变路线。要让这种情况发生，唯一办法是美国最高层发挥领导作用，因为无论谁获胜，都会希望特朗普站在自己一边。

一年前的停火、人质回归和20点框架是一项重大成就。特朗普政府可以利用这一周年和以色列选举来推进。否则，以色列可能重新滑回10月6日的现实：一个被遏制、被管控的哈马斯在平静表象背后悄然重建，随时准备再次爆发。
zhParas: 以色列人仍在争论，最近的那则报道是否属实——阿拉伯联合酋长国是否在10月7日屠杀发生前约10天，就警告过以色列哈马斯即将发动袭击。
但把目光死盯在10月7日之前的这几天上，会掩盖一个更深层的缺陷：以色列人的思维方式和战略构想基本没有改变，那就是冲突管理。以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。通过不让任何替代方案出现，它把巴勒斯坦问题整个边缘化了。
如果说大屠杀以来犹太人遭遇的最惨重灾难本应改变一件事，那就应该是这一点。然而，剥去“全面胜利”的说辞，以色列今天的加沙政策看上去并无二致，只是流血更多、废墟更多。
近几周，以色列领导人誓言要长期留在加沙，并彻底终结哈马斯的统治。在接连成功暗杀哈马斯指挥官之后，总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）和国防部长伊斯雷尔·卡茨（Israel Katz）宣称：“我们的信息很明确：没有哪个恐怖分子可以豁免，哈马斯不会留在加沙。”
以色列正以被削弱、被威慑住的哈马斯统治加沙为借口，加深加沙与由巴勒斯坦权力机构管辖的约旦河西岸之间的裂痕。
削弱哈马斯是正当的，以色列要求其放弃对加沙的控制也是正当的。但以色列显露出的实际偏好却讲述了另一个故事。
尽管以色列控制着加沙约60%的地区，哈马斯仍控制着当地95%以上的人口。哈马斯既是恐怖组织，也是加沙事实上的政府；要铲除前者，就必须为后者提供替代方案。以色列拒绝把这一角色交给巴勒斯坦权力机构，但去年却签署了特朗普（Trump）总统的20点计划，而该计划提供的正是这一点：过渡到技术官僚性质的加沙行政管理全国委员会，最终走向改革后的巴勒斯坦权力机构。
以色列政府显然从未打算让这一替代方案出现。
加沙管理国家委员会成员仍留在开罗，没有进入加沙的时间表。大约6000名经过审查的警察新兵本应在数月前开始训练，但因以色列不愿承诺允许他们返回，至今未能离开加沙。
国际稳定部队基地的建设因官僚程序而停滞。以色列控制的“绿区”本意是展示非哈马斯治理，其重建毫无进展。在约旦河西岸，以色列的政策正削弱巴勒斯坦权力机构，使其走向崩溃，并将该地区切割成一块块飞地，以确保无论有无加沙，巴勒斯坦治理都永远无法可行。
哈马斯也不出所料地拖延了这一计划。但8月它接受了和平委员会的路线图，列出15项原则，以分阶段解除武装换取以色列国防军撤离。以色列的担忧不无道理，包括路线图的时间表、解除武装的范围，以及卡塔尔和土耳其在核查遵守情况方面的作用。
未来的以色列政府若想取得不同的结果，就必须以相应的方式行事。
但合理的怀疑并不能成为拒绝接触的借口。以色列没有迫使哈马斯兑现其言辞，反而实际上赋予其对这一进程的否决权，因拖延而招致国际指责，而哈马斯则获得合法伙伴的认可。
国内政治在很大程度上解释了这一切。以色列将于10月27日举行一场激烈的选举，内塔尼亚胡的联盟无法在加沙问题上展现妥协。就连特朗普施压也对他有利，因为他声称只有他才能顶住他所称的“以色列国在白宫有史以来最伟大的朋友”。与此同时，内塔尼亚胡的对手正试图从右翼包抄他，誓言继续战斗，而非参与美国主导的计划。

items.title: Connecting the fight: AFA 2026 panel explores next-generation DAF battle management
items.author: Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth
items.summary: As the Department of the Air Force works to build a more connected and resilient Battle Network, military and industry leaders focused on one central challenge: how to move capability to the warfighter faster.
items.body:
Published Sept. 21, 2026

By Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth

Secretary of the Air Force Public Affairs

As the Department of the Air Force works to build a more connected and resilient Battle Network , military and industry leaders focused on one central challenge: how to move capability to the warfighter faster during a panel at the Air and Space Forces Association’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference, Sept. 15.

The “Next-Generation Battle Management” panel brought together Elaine Bitonti of Collins Aerospace; retired Maj. Gen. Scott Jobe with Boeing; retired Col. Sean Lowe with SAIC; and retired Maj. Luke Savoie with Elbit America. Brig. Gen. Joshua Williams , the Department of the Air Force portfolio acquisition executive for Command, Control, Communications and Battle Management, moderated the panel.

Williams opened by emphasizing the need to move beyond systems that operate independently of one another.

“The Department of the Air Force will not accept business models built on closed software stacks, black box hardware or restricted data interfaces,” Williams said. “The government must own and govern the technical baseline to ensure rapid iterative upgrades.”

For Savoie, that openness must extend from architecture to technology operating at the edge of the fight.

“How do you solve the compute portion on the edge, so that these tools and the connected network is working further and further forward and faster and faster within the loop of the folks that are on the front edge?” Savoie asked.

Bitonti connected that challenge directly to the movement of data across the force.

“I think first, you know, we understand from a battle management perspective, it’s all about how we’re moving the data,” Bitonti said, explaining that separating software from hardware and creating flexible communications architectures can allow systems to adapt as new requirements emerge.

That flexibility, the panelists agreed, is only useful if the DAF can test and field new capabilities quickly.

“One of the keys I think for the government is rapid prototyping, demonstrations and ensuring that we have industry partnerships,” Jobe said. “In order to really prove it to the DAF Battle Network or to the Joint Force, you got to go out there and demonstrate it, show that it’s real.”

Jobe pointed to a recent example in which an AMRAAM was launched from an MQ-28 Ghost Bat and integrated with an E-7 Wedgetail and F/A-18 Hornet within nine months.

“So that’s one example of the many things we’re doing and the rapid prototyping and getting to the field to demonstrate capabilities,” Jobe said.

The panel then turned to one of the biggest barriers between development and operational use: testing, security and accreditation.

Lowe described a process where software can move through development, security compliance, developmental testing and operational testing in sequence, with each transition potentially adding weeks or months.

“This is how you get months and years of delay,” Lowe said. He pointed to an approach where developmental and operational testers work alongside developers, allowing changes to be identified and addressed much earlier. “By putting the DTOT folks in the right places, particularly with the developmental teams, we can accelerate this.”

“The ATO process is … one, it’s out of control of most of the people in program office, and when you get to it, it does bring everything to a screeching halt,” Savoie said, calling for a broader examination of cybersecurity, information technology security and accreditation processes.

Jobe similarly pointed to the security environment as an area where policy and decision-making could move faster.

“I think we could probably move a lot faster,” Jobe said. “Maybe some communication and education to the personnel that are inside the acquisition system might be beneficial.”

For Bitonti, data sharing between services and coalition partners presents another policy challenge.

“We talk about really wanting to operate as a joint force and also with our coalition partners, but there are multiple restrictions, policy restrictions on rule sets of what data we can and can’t share,” she said.

“At this point, it’s not actually a technological impediment that is causing some of our struggles sharing data. It’s policy impediments.”

As the panel closed, Williams brought the discussion back to the DAF’s responsibility to deliver capability at the pace required by an evolving fight.

“Acquisition is a warfighting function,” Williams said. “We must deliver open, resilient, software-driven capability at the speed of operational relevance.”
items.titleZh: 打通作战链路：AFA 2026专题讨论会探讨下一代DAF战斗管理
items.summaryZh: 随着空军部（DAF）致力于构建一个更加互联、更具韧性的战斗网络，军方和业界领袖聚焦于一个核心挑战：如何更快地把能力送到作战人员手中。
items.zhFull:
发布于2026年9月21日

作者：Senior Airman Malia Heemsoth

空军部长公共事务办公室

在空军部着力构建更加互联、更具韧性的“战斗网络”（Battle Network）之际，军方和业界领袖于9月15日在空军与太空军协会“空中、太空与网络大会”的一场专题讨论上，聚焦一个核心难题：如何更快地把作战能力送到作战人员手中。

“下一代战斗管理”专题讨论汇集了柯林斯航空航天公司的Elaine Bitonti、波音公司的退役Maj. Gen. Scott Jobe、SAIC公司的退役Col. Sean Lowe，以及埃尔比特美国公司的退役Maj. Luke Savoie。空军部负责指挥、控制、通信与战斗管理组合采办事务的Brig. Gen. Joshua Williams主持了讨论。

Williams在开场发言中强调，必须超越那些各自独立运行的系统。

Williams说：“空军部不会接受建立在封闭软件栈、黑箱硬件或受限数据接口之上的商业模式。政府必须拥有并管理技术基线，以确保快速迭代升级。”

在Savoie看来，这种开放性必须从体系架构延伸到在作战前沿运行的技术。

“你如何解决边缘的计算部分，从而使这些工具和互联网络在最前沿人员的循环中越来越靠前、越来越快地运行？”萨沃伊（Savoie）问道。

比通蒂（Bitonti）将这一挑战直接与部队中数据的移动联系起来。

“我认为，首先，你知道，从战斗管理角度看，我们明白关键在于我们如何移动数据，”比通蒂说，并解释称，将软件与硬件分离并创建灵活的通信架构，可以让系统在新需求出现时进行适应。

小组成员一致认为，这种灵活性只有在DAF能够快速测试和部署新能力时才有用。

“我认为，对政府而言，关键之一在于快速原型开发、演示，并确保我们拥有行业合作伙伴关系，”乔布（Jobe）说。“为了真正向DAF战斗网络或联合部队证明它，你必须走出去演示它，表明它是真实的。”

乔布指出最近的一个例子：一枚AMRAAM从一架MQ-28 Ghost Bat上发射，并在九个月内与一架E-7 Wedgetail和F/A-18 Hornet完成集成。

“因此，这只是我们所做众多事情中的一个例子，也是快速原型开发和进入实地演示能力的一个例子，”乔布说。

随后，小组转向研发与作战使用之间最大的障碍之一：测试、安全和认证。

洛(Lowe)描述了一个流程：软件会依次经过开发、安全合规、开发测试和作战测试，而每一次转段都可能增加数周或数月的时间。

“这就是为什么会出现数月乃至数年的延误，”洛(Lowe)说。他提到一种做法，即开发测试和作战测试人员与开发人员并肩工作，从而使变更能够更早被发现和解决。“把开发测试与作战测试人员放到合适的位置，尤其是与开发团队在一起，我们就能加快这一进程。”

“ATO流程……其一，它不受项目办公室大多数人的控制，而一旦进入这一环节，确实会让一切戛然而止，”萨沃伊(Savoie)说，并呼吁对网络安全、信息技术安全和认证流程进行更广泛的审视。

乔布(Jobe)同样指出，安全环境是一个政策和决策可以更快推进的领域。

“我认为我们很可能可以快得多，”乔布说。“也许对采办系统内的人员进行一些沟通和教育可能会有所裨益。”

对比通蒂(Bitonti)而言，各军种与联盟伙伴之间的数据共享构成了另一项政策挑战。

“我们谈到非常希望作为联合部队行动，也与我们的联盟伙伴共同行动，但在关于我们可以和不能共享哪些数据的规则集方面，存在多重限制，也就是政策限制，”她说。

“目前，造成我们在共享数据方面一些困难的，实际上并不是技术障碍。而是政策障碍。”

在专题讨论结束时，Williams 把讨论拉回到空军部（DAF）的职责上，即以不断演变的作战所要求的速度交付能力。

“采办是一项作战职能，”Williams 说。“我们必须以作战相关性所需的速度，交付开放、有韧性、软件驱动的能力。”

items.title: Never Underestimate the Houthis
items.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels are in a position to shape the next phase of the conflict between the United States and Iran if they attempt to renew their blockade of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. And no one should assume that a deal with Iran will bind what the Houthis do next.
items.body:
Just a few years ago, Yemen's Houthi rebels were second- or third-tier members of Iran's “Axis of Resistance,” prompting policymakers to treat them as a subsidiary of Tehran. But while they benefit from Iranian weapons, training and know-how, the Houthis also have their own interests at heart—and behave accordingly.

This armed group that controls much of northern Yemen is in position to shape the next phase of the conflict between the United States and Iran if they attempt to renew their blockade of the Bab al-Mandab Strait. The Houthis could reignite the war in Yemen, scuttle efforts to make a deal with Iran and draw the United States even deeper into the region's conflicts.

A key assumption going into the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran, which began in February, was that Iran's proxy militias had been critically weakened. Hezbollah, the militant group in Lebanon that was once Iran's most powerful partner in the region, suffered heavy blows from Israel during the Gaza war, as did Hamas. Iran lost another key ally when Bashar al-Assad's regime in Syria collapsed in December 2024.

The Houthis, whose military capacity had also been weakened by U.S. strikes in 2024–25, did not jump back into the fray right away when the United States and Israel began striking Iran this year, seemingly sparing them similar blows.

Perhaps they were biding their time. Because of a quirk of geography, the Houthis are able to disrupt commercial traffic in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a choke point at the entry to the Red Sea, through which 12 percent to 15 percent of maritime trade travels. At the other end of the Red Sea lies the Suez Canal, a vital route for oil and liquefied natural gas headed to North American and European markets. With Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, the Houthis are now in an unusually powerful position.

With Iran effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz, the Houthis are now in an unusually powerful position.

They have come far in global influence since seizing Yemen's capital, Sanaa, in 2014 and expelling the internationally recognized government from the city in early 2015. When the rebel forces pushed south in March of that year, in an attempt to take over territory in southern Yemen, a coalition led by Saudi Arabia and backed by the United States intervened.

The once localized war became a regional conflict and a devastating humanitarian crisis. Finally, facing a stalemate and significant international pressure, both sides agreed to a U.N.-brokered cease-fire in April 2022. By that point, the Houthis had created a de facto state in northern Yemen, while the weak Saudi-backed government nominally ruled parts of the south and west.

The Houthis flexed their muscles by attacking shipping vessels in the Red Sea early in the Israel-Gaza war that started in 2023. Using low-cost, low-tech equipment like one-way attack drones, missiles and unmanned surface vessels, the Houthis made the crossing more dangerous, driving up the cost of insuring commercial ships as much as twentyfold, effectively closing the strait. The only alternate route forced ships around the southern tip of the African continent, an extra 4,000 or more nautical miles, increasing shipping costs.

Last month, the Houthis resumed attacks on Red Sea shipping, striking Saudi-linked commercial oil tankers and hitting Saudi energy and transportation infrastructure. They were responding to what they claimed were Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa Airport's runway on July 13, seemingly in an effort to prevent an incoming Iranian flight from landing. For now, commercial ships continue to transit the Red Sea, although tanker traffic has declined substantially over the past month. Houthi attacks have also continued on ships the group claims are Saudi-aligned, and an attack on a cargo ship on Aug. 12 included the first reported fatalities of this latest round of attacks.

In recent days, the Houthis have claimed attacks on a ship in the Red Sea port of Mokha, which is held by forces allied with the internationally recognized government of Yemen, and on airports and oil refinery infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

With the effective closure of Hormuz, the Red Sea-Suez route has become even more important. Most notably, Saudi Arabia had sought to avoid Hormuz by routing crude oil via a pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu on its western coast. The new Houthi attacks have disrupted that option. The near closure of both Hormuz and the Suez routes could compound problems for global trade, pushing the cost of oil and inflation even higher.

Now the Houthis are positioned to step up their involvement in an already raging regional conflagration, complicating efforts to end it. Some may assume that this move is at the behest of Iran, but the reality is likely more complicated.

Highly attuned to their own interests and pragmatic in the international arena, the Houthis have proved savvy at choosing when to enter or escalate conflicts. When they attacked shipping in the Red Sea in 2023–25, for example, they said it was to pressure Israel to de-escalate its operations in Gaza. The strikes also bolstered their legitimacy in the territory they control in northern Yemen, diverting attention from their governance failures at a time when their popularity had eroded.

The Houthis have proved savvy at choosing when to enter or escalate conflicts.

This time, the Houthis appear to see an opening to gain leverage in negotiations with Saudi Arabia to reach a political settlement in the Yemeni war—or an opportunity to resume attacks against the internationally backed government.

The previous round of Houthi attacks, in 2023–25, had a significant but ultimately manageable effect on the global economy. Estimates suggested that the ensuing shipping disruptions would have a small impact on inflation. The economic effects of closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the same time as Hormuz are likely to be more dire.

While the United States looks to wind down the war with Iran, the Houthis are threatening to resume their war in Yemen, which would likely draw in Saudi Arabia, menace the global oil trade and keep the region unstable.

It will be difficult to de-escalate regional tensions without addressing the Houthis' threat directly, rather than assuming it can be resolved by dealing with their supposed boss, Iran. At the same time, no one should assume that a deal with Iran will bind what the Houthis do next. The international community should confront them as a pragmatic and dangerous actor making decisions in their own self-interest.
items.titleZh: 永远不要低估胡塞武装
items.summaryZh: 如果也门胡塞武装试图重启对曼德海峡的封锁，他们就有能力塑造美国与伊朗之间冲突的下一阶段走向。而且任何人都不应以为与伊朗达成协议就能约束胡塞武装接下来的行动。
items.zhFull:
就在几年前，也门胡塞叛军还只是伊朗“抵抗轴心”中的二线或三线成员，这促使政策制定者将其视为德黑兰的附属。然而，尽管他们受益于伊朗的武器、训练和技术，胡塞武装也有自己的利益考量，并据此行事。

这支控制也门北部大片地区的武装组织，如果试图重启对曼德海峡的封锁，就有能力影响美国与伊朗冲突的下一阶段。胡塞武装可能重新点燃也门战争，破坏与伊朗达成协议的努力，并把美国进一步拖入该地区的冲突。

在2月开始的美以对伊朗袭击中，一个关键假设是伊朗的代理民兵已遭到严重削弱。黎巴嫩激进组织真主党曾是伊朗在该地区最强大的伙伴，在加沙战争期间遭到以色列重创，哈马斯也是如此。2024年12月，叙利亚巴沙尔·阿萨德 (Bashar al-Assad) 政权垮台，伊朗又失去一个关键盟友。

胡塞武装的军事能力也曾因美国在2024—25年的打击而遭到削弱；当美国和以色列今年开始打击伊朗时，他们并未立即重新加入战团，似乎因此免遭类似打击。

也许他们是在等待时机。由于地理上的特殊条件，胡塞武装能够扰乱曼德海峡的商业航运；这条海峡是红海入口处的咽喉要道，12%至15%的海上贸易经此通行。红海另一端是苏伊士运河，这是石油和液化天然气运往北美和欧洲市场的重要通道。随着伊朗实际上封锁霍尔木兹海峡，胡塞武装如今处于异常强大的地位。

随着伊朗实际上封锁霍尔木兹海峡，胡塞武装如今处于异常强大的地位。

自2014年夺取也门首都萨那，并于2015年初将国际公认的政府赶出该市以来，他们在全球影响力方面已取得长足进展。当年3月，叛军向南推进，试图夺取也门南部领土，沙特阿拉伯领导、美国支持的联军随即介入。

这场一度局部化的战争演变为地区冲突和毁灭性的人道主义危机。最终，面对僵局和巨大的国际压力，双方于2022年4月同意接受联合国斡旋的停火。到那时，胡塞武装已在也门北部建立了一个事实上的国家，而沙特支持的软弱政府名义上统治着南部和西部的部分地区。

胡塞武装在2023年爆发的以色列-加沙战争初期通过袭击红海航运船只来展示实力。他们使用单向攻击无人机、导弹和无人水面艇等低成本、低技术装备，使这一航道穿越变得更加危险，将商船保险费率推高至原来的二十倍之多，实际上封锁了该海峡。唯一的替代航线迫使船只绕行非洲大陆南端，额外航行4,000 nautical miles以上，推高了航运成本。

上个月，胡塞武装恢复对红海航运的袭击，打击与沙特有关联的商用油轮，并袭击沙特的能源和交通基础设施。他们称此举是对沙特7月13日空袭萨那机场跑道的回应，后者似乎意在阻止一架即将抵达的伊朗航班降落。目前，商船仍在继续穿行红海，尽管过去一个月油轮运输量大幅下降。胡塞武装还继续袭击其声称与沙特结盟的船只，而8月12日对一艘货船的袭击中出现了本轮袭击中首批报告的死亡事件。

近日，胡塞武装声称袭击了红海摩卡港的一艘船只——该港由与也门国际公认政府结盟的武装力量控制——以及沙特阿拉伯的机场和炼油厂基础设施。

随着霍尔木兹海峡实际关闭，红海—苏伊士航线变得更加重要。最突出的是，沙特阿拉伯曾试图通过管道将原油输送至其西海岸的延布港，以避开霍尔木兹海峡。胡塞武装的新一轮袭击使这一选择受阻。霍尔木兹海峡和红海—苏伊士航线近乎同时关闭，可能使全球贸易问题雪上加霜，进一步推高油价和通胀。

如今，胡塞武装已有条件加大介入这场本已熊熊燃烧的地区冲突，使结束冲突的努力更加复杂。一些人可能认为此举是应伊朗指使，但实际情况可能更为复杂。

胡塞武装高度关注自身利益，在国际舞台上行事务实，在何时介入或升级冲突的问题上表现出精明的判断力。例如，在2023—2025年袭击红海航运时，他们称此举是为了向以色列施压，促使其缓和在加沙的军事行动。这些袭击还增强了其在也门北部所控制地区的合法性，在其支持率下滑之际转移了人们对其治理失败的注意力。

胡塞武装在何时介入或升级冲突的问题上表现得相当精明。

这一次，胡塞武装似乎看到了在与沙特阿拉伯谈判中获取筹码、推动也门战争政治解决的机会——或者是恢复对国际社会支持的政府发动袭击的契机。

上一轮胡塞武装袭击（2023—2025年）对全球经济造成了显著但最终尚可消化的影响。当时的评估认为，随之而来的航运中断对通胀的影响有限。而一旦曼德海峡与霍尔木兹海峡同时被封锁，其经济后果可能更为严峻。

在美国寻求结束与伊朗的战争之际，胡塞武装却威胁要在也门重启战事，这很可能把沙特阿拉伯卷入其中，威胁全球石油贸易，并使该地区持续动荡不安。

如果不直接应对胡塞武装的威胁，而是想当然地认为通过与其所谓的后台伊朗打交道就能解决问题，那么缓和地区紧张局势将十分困难。与此同时，任何人都不应以为与伊朗达成协议就能约束胡塞武装接下来的行动。国际社会应当把他们视为一个务实而危险、依据自身利益行事的行动方来加以应对。

items.title: Preserving Jobs and Tax Revenue in the Age of AI: Q&A with Carter Price
items.summary: Carter Price, a mathematician at RAND and co-director of the RAND Von Furstenberg Family Budget Model Initiative, discusses ways to rebalance the tax code so that it doesn't incentivize employers to replace humans with AI.
items.body:
If AI starts to replace jobs, it isn't just American workers who will feel the loss of income. So will the U.S. Treasury.

Nearly two-thirds of all federal revenue comes from taxes levied on human labor, a recent RAND study noted. That revenue will not be easy to make up if AI starts to put large numbers of people out of work.

Carter Price has been looking for ways to rebalance the tax code so that it doesn't incentivize employers to replace humans with AI. He's a mathematician at RAND and co-director of the RAND Von Furstenberg Family Budget Model Initiative. And he has an idea for how to give workers an edge in the age of AI.

How does the existing tax code disincentivize keeping human workers on the job?

We went through all 7,000 pages of the tax code with a tool we built as part of the RAND Budget Model Initiative. It allows us to identify every provision, every line item, and its implications. There's a lot in there. But we identified several places where the existing U.S tax code works against companies hiring or keeping workers.

The employer payroll tax is one obvious example. Companies have to pay that tax for every worker they hire, so more workers means more expense. Meanwhile, the tax code allows companies to write off the depreciation of big, expensive assets early, before those assets actually wear out. That can make buying something like a robotic system much more cost-effective—which makes that tax write-off a direct subsidy for displacing human workers.

What's your idea to change the incentives here?

You and I pay progressive taxes on our income. That means if we make more money, we move into a higher tax bracket.

Our idea is somewhat similar, but for companies. The government would tax high corporate profits per worker in addition to taxing their income overall.

Imagine a company makes $1 million in profit and has 100 employees. Its profit per worker is $10,000. Now let's say that company brings in a lot of AI and lays off all but ten of its workers. Now its profit per worker is $100,000, and it just moved into a higher tax bracket. It's going to pay more in taxes for that same $1 million in profit.

AI might still be so much more efficient that it still makes sense for some companies to replace those workers. This tax structure wouldn't stand in the way of that.

But where the current tax code sometimes disincentivizes keeping human workers, our proposed change would flip the script. It would put the tax code more on the side of workers instead of on the side of AI and automation.

What else did your tax code analysis find that could help promote employment?

We found a lot of special, niche provisions that are just scattered throughout the tax code. You could eliminate those and really clean everything up. There are three different clean-energy vehicle tax provisions, for example, and they all do pretty much the same thing.

These niche provisions pointed us to a suite of changes that could really make a difference. The government could eliminate those special tax breaks. That would bring in additional revenue.

The federal government could then eliminate the employer payroll tax and replace it with two business taxes: one a flat tax on business revenue, and the other the per-worker tax on high profits.

Companies would be no worse off. The government would balance the loss of revenue from eliminating the payroll tax with an increase from eliminating special tax carve-outs. And we'd be incentivizing human employment instead of using tax breaks to incentivize things like investments in distilled spirits.

Our proposed change would put the tax code more on the side of workers instead of on the side of AI and automation.

What would it take to implement those changes?

It takes an act of Congress to change the Internal Revenue Code. But that's a low barrier compared to what some other popular policy ideas that are floating around would face. For example, a value-added tax, which would be like a nationwide sales tax, would require an entirely new tax-collection infrastructure. And a federal wealth tax, which could generate revenue from huge concentrations of wealth, would require a constitutional amendment in addition to new tax-collection infrastructure.

By contrast, policymakers could at least theoretically wake up tomorrow and pass a law that would make the tax code more robust by reducing its dependence on income from labor.

Furthermore, simplifying the tax code would give people back millions of hours that they currently spend filling out forms. It would improve the efficiency of the economy, and that's something everyone can like.

What motivates you to do this work?

I'm a mathematician. And there have been a lot of headlines about the advances that AI models have made in mathematics in particular. AI can generate code that would take a human hours, or even days, to write. I'm biased, but I think human mathematicians still provide a lot of value that AI can't fully replace. I'm not sure that will be true forever. But until that changes, we shouldn't rush into replacing workers with AI, and our tax code certainly shouldn't incentivize employers to do so.

items.body:
The Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) has five unique ionizing radiation sources. All sources are maintained and operated by the Survivable Electronics Technology group (AFRL/RJSV) at Kirtland AFB, NM. These sources allow partnering researchers from industry, government labs, and universities to study a wide spectrum of total ionizing dose and prompt dose effects. The Survivable Electronics Technology group primarily uses these sources to determine the effects of radiation on advanced microelectronics, photonics, sensors, and micro-electromechanical systems needed for Air Force, Space Force, Department of Defense, and government space and missile systems .

Dosimetry; both CaF 2 and Ion Chambers

Fabricate test board and boxes for devices under test

Machine Shop access

B1500 w/ Switching Matrix

Mixed Signal Tester

Gamma Radiation Sources

The Cobalt-60 source can deliver a maximum total ionizing dose of ~20 krad (Si)/min to a minimum of <1 rad (Si)/min (which falls within ASTM 1019 specs of 300 to 50 rad(Si)/sec). Slightly higher dose rates may be attained if researchers are willing to accept that the source will appear as a line source opposed to a point source. This source produces two energy peaks at 1.17 and 1.33 MeV. The irradiator is a 360-degree panoramic irradiator, facility area is 1,500 ft 2 which provides the researcher the benefit of a large range of variable dose rates with plenty of area to conduct experiments. Evaluation of subsystems is possible in this cell. The large area of the facility minimizes the possibility of dose enhancement due to scatter. The high energy photons give a uniform dose deposition throughout the sample of interest. AFRL Co-60 facility provides the capability of performing in-situ experiments whereby measurements on components are taken during gamma irradiation through the use of 120 ft of BNC cables and CAT-5 cables that would allow the experimenters to control computer-controlled instrumentation from the control room to the irradiation test cell.

Total Dose Simulator

1.17 & 1.33 MeV Gammas

<.001 to 20 krad(Si)/min

1500 ft 2 of Test Cell

360-degree panoramic irradiator

The Cesium 137 low dose rate source will deliver a maximum of 40 rad(Si)/hr or a minimum of 0.3 rad(Si)/hr. This source produces gamma rays with a single energy peak at 662 keV. The Cs-137 source is capable of housing experiments which can fit in 1 ft 3 of volume. Due to the small exposure volume, a Pb/Al box is required for all experiments performed in this source to eliminate a dose enhancement effect. Will provide a Pb/Al box for experiments which meets ASTM standards if users do not have one. This source is capable of providing in-situ experimentation.

Low Total Dose Simulator

662 keV Gammas

0.005 to 0.667 rad(Si)/min

2.25 ft 2 Test Cell

X-Ray Radiation Sources

The ARACOR X-ray test system is used to investigate total ionizing dose effects on individual microelectronic devices. This system produces X-rays with energies that have a max range of 60 keV with peak energies at 10 keV and dose rates ranging from 0.1 to 30 krad (SiO 2 )/min. The system is capable to accommodating an 8” wafer for X-ray characterization of fabricated die or packaged devices with lids removed. Capable of utilizing a probe card to probe and bias up to 48 contacts concurrently.

10 to 60 keV spectrum, peak 10 keV

0.1 to 30 krad (SiO 2 )/min

Low Energy X-Ray (LEXR)

The Low Energy X-ray source is a Comet MXR-160/22 constant potential X-ray system which produces X-rays with energies that have a max range of 10 keV to 160 keV and peaks at 10 keV and 60 keV depending on the applied voltage. This source can produce a total ionizing dose rate of 360 krad (SiO 2 )/min. Exposure area is a 1.84 cm diameter at 10 cm from the X-ray tube. The distance from the tube can be varied up to 1 m to control dose rate. The X-ray tube current is variable in order to control dose rate, and the total energy deposited per unit area. This source is capable of providing in-situ experimentation.

High Total Dose Simulator

10 to 160 keV spectrum, peaks 10 and 60 keV(adjustable)

360 krad(SiO 2 )/min (max)

30 ft 2 Test Cell

Flash X-Ray (FXR)

The Flash X-ray source is a Febetron 705 machine which produces prompt dose exposures simulating nuclear weapons environments. This facility is capable of producing a 20 nanosecond pulse X-ray. The average 2.1 MeV of the X-rays produced in this facility provides a dose rate output from between 1x10 7 to 2x10 11 rad (Si)/sec. A 70 ft 2 . screen room is available for housing experiments in order to minimize the effects of EMP produced by the Febetron 705. To obtain higher dose rates, experiments may be performed in open air directly in front of the Febetron 705.

High Dose Simulator

X-ray Mode (Prompt dose)

1x10 7 to 2x10 11 rad(Si)/sec X-ray
